Mysticism changes what is inside every school of magic. About three hundred spells are taught by tomes, and a handful of those are held, which is covered in episode three. Here are some to look out for. In Restoration, Heal Other comes at Apprentice level, then Close Greater Wounds at Adept, then Breath of Life and Stendarr's Mercy. There are also three circles you place on the ground, called Circle of Life, Circle of Wisdom and Circle of Strength. They restore health, magicka or stamina around a spot, and whether they reach other players is not yet tested in multiplayer. In Destruction, look for Vampiric Touch and Vampiric Bolt, which steal health. In Alteration, look for Feather and Corrode Armor. In Illusion, look for Paralysis, which has moved there, and the morale spells Courage, Rally and Call to Arms. In Conjuration, look for Conjure Skeleton and Conjure Skeleton Archer.

Where do you buy them? Our mod guide says you buy them from the usual vendors and spell tomes. Which vendor stocks which spell has not been confirmed, and the fact that a tome exists does not prove that a vendor sells it. So when you walk into a shop, read the list.
Next, racial goals.

As episode five explained, Imperious gives each race a power that you earn by meeting a goal, instead of having it from the first minute. Six races have goals that lead to a power the group permits. Argonians earn Caustic Spit, a strong debuff on enemy armor and magic resistance, by finding four underwater chests. Bretons earn Shared Ancestry by discovering ten standing stones, and it lets them borrow another race's power for five minutes, though the group's holds still apply to whatever they borrow. Imperials earn Colovian Star after twenty quests. Khajiit earn Perception, longer night vision, after collecting fifty thousand gold over their lifetime. Nords earn Avatar after clearing eight dungeons. Orcs earn Berserk after one hundred and fifty Shockwave staggers. Whether progress toward these goals shows up properly for every player has not been tested in multiplayer, so keep your own count.

A reminder for two other races. In revision seven, our own small patch gives High Elves Highborn and Redguards Adrenaline Rush, and we tested both in single-player on October fourth. That test found that the powers appear, can be cast, keep their daily cooldown, survive a reload, and show up on test characters made before the patch too. They have not been tested in multiplayer. Dark Elves and Wood Elves still have no racial power that the group permits.
Now perks worth reading again.

Better Vanilla Perks keeps the eighteen trees, but rewrites what many perks do. A few that are worth finding. Armsman, the first One Handed perk, now adds critical chance as well as damage. Each Restoration cost-saving perk adds a magicka regeneration effect that grows as you climb, and Master Restoration makes every Restoration spell half again as efficient. Heavy and Light Armor set bonuses work with three matching pieces instead of four. In Speech, the first Dragonborn rank gives better prices and one extra skill level every time you read a skill book. In Alchemy, Green Thumb gives you two ingredients from each plant. In Conjuration, Summoner and Puppeteer add range as well as capacity. And a Nord can buy Intimidation to get Battlecry, though that costs a perk and is not the original free power. Always read the description before you spend a point, and remember that a description is not a measured result.

Now gear, if you like dressing the part. Three optional mods add craftable gear. Playable Greybeard Robes adds a robe, hood and boots, Wizard Hats adds hats in many colors, and a Lord of the Rings weapon collection adds swords and axes. Ask who has them, because a friend without them will not see the gear.
Now the map.

Atlas Map Markers adds hundreds of markers that Skyrim leaves out, such as shrines, camps and landmarks. Everyone sees the same markers, and you can turn categories on and off in Mod Configuration. When you are looking for something to go and find, open the map first. But you cannot fast travel by clicking the map, because Disable Fast Travel switches that off. You walk, or take a carriage or a ferry, which should still work but have not been tested.
Last, what revision seven adds to the world. None of it has been tested with several players yet.

Cathedral Weathers and Seasons makes the weather moodier, with fog, thunder and darker nights. The mod's page describes a power called Cathedral Meditation, where you can adjust how dark the nights are. Weather is shared across the party, and the party leader's game decides it.

Sounds of Skyrim Complete adds about four hundred and sixty ambient sounds, with its Cathedral patch so the two fit together. Listen for wolves and ravens at night, dripping and echoing caves, moaning undead in draugr dungeons, Falmer screams, storms heard from cave mouths, and noise in towns. Sound is played on each player's own computer, so there is nothing to sync.

Random Dragons No More switches off the random dragon attacks that ordinary Skyrim sets off every few days. Dragons that belong to the story, and dragons that are placed in the world, are meant to remain. So in our game, a dragon should be somewhere you go to find, not something that jumps you on the road. Expect to meet fewer dragons overall, and so probably fewer dragon souls.
The Notice Board puts job boards outside inns. The leader takes a job and everyone goes along, though the others may not see the job in their journals.

Vampire Attacks Restored brings vampire attacks to towns and villages at night, outside the walled cities. None happen before level twelve, and they become more likely as you level up. So be ready when you walk into a village after dark.

Simplest Survival adds hunger and thirst. About thirty real minutes after you last ate or drank, your health, magicka and stamina regeneration drops to half, until you eat food or drink a potion. So bring both.

And one more thing to try. At your first quest hand-in, write down each player's gold, items and skills before and after. Nobody has tested who receives quest rewards in multiplayer, and your own notes will settle it faster than any guide.
That is the end of this episode.
